description.value: A tiny 3-site campground on the south shore of Bridge Lake, offering open shoreline for paddling, swimming, and fishing amid bald eagle nests and beaver colonies; no drinking water (well decommissioned due to arsenic).

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The BC Parks website confirms this is an active provincial campground on the south end of Bridge Lake, ~50 km east of 100 Mile House on Hwy 24. The site explicitly states 'There is no drinking water available. Due to arsenic concerns, the well used for drinking water has been decommissioned.' — confirming potable water as false. The page mentions Bridge Lake General Store nearby (in the context of the nearest public telephone), which as a general store would stock basic food items. No explicit confirmation that this specific campground accepts reservations (the reservation links appear to be general BC Parks informational pages). No mention of hiker/biker sites, showers, or other cyclist-specific amenities.
concerns: No drinking water available — cyclists must carry or treat their own water
No specific phone number or street address available for this campground
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active BC Parks campground on Highway 24, a key east-west corridor in the Cariboo. Useful overnight stop for touring cyclists despite lack of potable water.

wow_evidence: open shoreline for paddling, swimming, and fishing
